title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
slides: Can Apple make AI health tools actually useful?
A new study targets how AI interprets health data
The surprise: most AI health advice fails real-world tests
Your next iPhone may flag risks before symptoms appear
Test one health query against your doctor's advice
thread_text:
1. AI health advice fails

A new study tested AI health tools in real-world scenarios. Most failed to match a doctor's advice. Apple wants to change that with the iPhone.

2. Apple's big bet

Apple is developing AI health tools for the iPhone that could flag risks before symptoms appear. The goal: make AI health advice actually useful.

3. The interpretation gap

AI often misreads health data because it lacks context. A new study targets how AI interprets symptoms, aiming to fix the root cause.

4. Your iPhone as watchdog

Imagine your phone warning you about a health risk days before you feel sick. That's the promise, but only if the AI can pass real-world tests.

5. Test your AI

Ask ChatGPT or another AI about a health symptom you've had. Compare its answer to your doctor's. Would you trust it?

instagram.caption:
Most AI health advice doesn't match what a doctor would tell you in real-world tests. 🩺

Apple is now running a study on how AI interprets health data, because the tool often misreads symptoms without context.

The goal is an iPhone that flags risks before symptoms show up.

If that works, your phone becomes a first check before you book an appointment — for you and for anyone who writes about health online.

Try it now: ask an AI about a symptom you've had, then compare it to your doctor's advice. Would you trust the answer? 🤔
